thread:
Elena: Heads-up — customer acme-inc reporting huge throughput drop on their Dedicated pool (pool-chi-2). 99th latency jumped from 120ms to 1.2s, and we see a lot of 429s and spikes in billed token count. Can we triage?
Ryan: grabbing logs now. which model variant + config? any recent rollout?
Elena: model = llama-3-8b-quant-v2, pinned. No recent canary from their side. Dedicated autoscale showed several quick scale-down/scale-up cycles around the time of spike.
Tony: autoscaler events + 429s could be retry amplification shrinking effective batch sizes. Do we have the request/response traces for a sample timeframe?
Maria: I pulled a 5m trace: a pattern of auth refresh failures (401) from the customer SDK, followed by immediate retries that set max_context_tokens=16 (client-side), so continuous-batcher ends up forming tiny micro-batches. Also saw KV cache miss rate jump. snippet: ```log
2026-02-12T15:03:06Z customer=acme-inc pool=pool-chi-2 req_id=gh12 auth=401 retry=1
2026-02-12T15:03:06Z batcher.evicted_prefill size=2 -> exec
2026-02-12T15:03:06Z batcher.exec tokens=32 latency=980ms
```
Sara: auth 401s -> retries -> small requested max tokens -> smaller batches -> higher per-token overhead -> billed tokens still count. That fits. Any idea what triggered auth refresh failures?
Elena: customer says they rotated their API key right at 15:02 and their deploy had a bug that retry loop didn't backoff.
Ryan: on infra side, I see scheduler quantum stayed at 8ms, but batch formation time increased from 6ms to 180ms due to waiting for KV fetches. Continuous batching had lots of tiny windows. Metrics: `batch_size_p50` dropped from 12 to 2, `tokens_per_batch_p50` from 512 to 40.
Tony: we should confirm whether autoscaler reacted to apparent drop in effective throughput and scaled down, making the hot shard noisier. If scaled-down GPUs had high tail latency, that could further fragment batches.
Maria: quick repro steps I used: 1) curl to hit the dedicated endpoint with an old API key to force 401 and immediate retry, 2) set client max_tokens small to mimic their SDK bug. Commands: ```bash
# simulate broken client
curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-3-8b-quant-v2","input":"hello","max_tokens":16}'
```
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled config patch `batching.tolerance.small_window=0.5` to canary on pool-chi-2 at 15:32 UTC.
Ryan: I tried a quick conservative mitigation: bumped `continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens` from 1024 -> 2048 and increased `batching.min_wait_ms` from 2 -> 10 on pool-chi-2 canary. Result: tokens_per_batch_p50 rose to ~384 within 30s, 99th latency dropped back to ~140ms.
Elena: did that affect tail error rates / cost? Tony: error 429s went down by 80% for acme-inc, but we saw a small temporary increase in queueing on other tenants on the same node until autoscaler rebalanced. Cost: minor — token efficiency improved so net billed tokens fell for the period.
Maria: longer-term fixes: 1) add a small randomized backoff on client SDK retry for 401/403, 2) have autoscaler ignore sub-minute transient dips caused by auth bursts (tweak hysteresis), 3) add a guard in continuous-batcher to avoid forming batches below a min_tokens threshold for dedicated pools with noisy-tenants flagged.
Tony: filed incident ticket INC-2026-291 with notes + repro. Suggest we contact acme-inc support lead and share recommended SDK patch.
Elena: I opened a support ticket to the customer, asked them to rotate keys correctly and push SDK patch. We'll keep the canary changes for 2 hours then roll back if stable.
Ryan: saved the traces and uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/incs/2317774444/traces.tar.gz
Sara: thumbs up. Also putting a quick alert rule to catch `batch_tokens_p50 < 50 AND 99p_latency > 500ms` so we can detect similar auth-induced microbatch storms.
Elena: great — keeping this thread open until autoscaler stabilizes. Will update after rollback window. :white_check_mark:
